sections.title: Event Overview
sections.body: PERMIRA Summer Camp 2026 (PERMIRA Camp 3.0 — III Indonesian–Russian Students Summer Camp) is a three-day youth diplomacy and cultural-exchange programme organised by PERMIRA St. Petersburg, the Indonesian Students' Association in Russia. It is held as part of the celebration of 76 years of Indonesia–Russia diplomatic relations and the Saint Petersburg Year of Culture. Theme: "Cuisine of Nusantara: Lessons of Nature and Friendship of Peoples". Dates: 19–21 July 2026. Location: Cape Kiperort — the largest peninsula reaching into Vyborg Bay (Gulf of Finland), in the Vyborgsky regional nature reserve, Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast. It has dry pine forests, a rocky western shore and a sandy eastern one, and rich coastal birdlife; the group reaches it overland by coach — pure focus on cooking, nature, and each other.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: The camp strengthens youth diplomacy between Indonesia and Russia, with ASEAN participation, focused on cultural, language, and historical exchange among students. It uses cuisine as an inclusive medium for cross-cultural collaboration, alongside an environmental-stewardship ethic (waste sorting, reduced single-use plastic, efficient food portions). It is a friendship and cultural programme — not an environmental conference.

sections.title: Participants
sections.body: Capacity is 35 students: 15 from Indonesia, 10 from Russia, and 10 from ASEAN countries. Participants are active university students in Russia (aged 18 or over, no upper limit), verified by a Russian university student card (Studencheskiy Bilet / Propusk), with basic conversational English. Indonesian participants must also be registered in the PERMIRA St. Petersburg database and have completed Indonesian citizen self-reporting (lapor diri).

sections.title: Getting there & meeting point
sections.body: On Day 1 (19 July), participants gather at Ozerki metro station in Saint Petersburg at 09:00 MSK, where volunteers will meet the group. Transfer to the camp runs 10:00–13:00 MSK by coach, travelling north to Cape Kiperort — a peninsula in the Vyborgsky nature reserve, Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast, on the shore of Vyborg Bay. Please arrive on time — the group travels together and latecomers cannot be accommodated. On arrival, each participant is shown to a tent labelled with their name in Russian and Indonesian, followed by a safety briefing in Russian with Indonesian and English translation.

sections.title: Programme
sections.body:
Day 1 (19 July) — Arrive & Open: 09:00 gather at Ozerki metro; 10:00–13:00 transfer by coach north to Cape Kiperort (a peninsula on Vyborg Bay); 13:00 tent placement and briefing; 13:30–14:35 bilingual opening ceremony; 14:35 lunch; 15:30 natural-materials masterclass; 17:00 cape walk and team formation; 19:00 guided free time; 20:00 dinner; 21:00 campfire team games; 23:00 rest.
Day 2 (20 July) — Cook & Connect: 08:00 morning exercise; 08:30 breakfast (Bubur Ayam); 09:30–13:00 PERMIRA Master Chef — an education & discussion session and a culinary masterclass (Nasi Goreng Kampung, Sate Taichan, Sambal Matah) with chef Aprilio Kristian Justin Teken; 13:30 lunch; 15:00–17:00 fusion cooking challenge (Indonesia 50%, Russia 30%, ASEAN 20%); 18:30 dinner; 19:30 open-air team games; 21:00 cultural night (PERMIRA's Got Talent); 23:00 heart-to-heart at the campfire; 01:00 rest.
Day 3 (21 July) — Reflect & Farewell: 08:00 morning exercise; 08:30 breakfast (Cekodok); 09:30–11:30 gotong-royong eco clean-up of Cape Kiperort and prep to leave; 11:30 time capsule (Wish Board); 12:30–13:00 closing ceremony with awards and group photo; 13:40 departure. (All times MSK.)

sections.title: Opening ceremony
sections.body: The official opening runs 13:30–14:35 MSK on 19 July, hosted bilingually by Indonesian and Russian presenters and broadcast live at summercamp2026.permiraspb.org. Programme: the national anthems of Indonesia and Russia; remarks from Prof. Dr. Pratikno, M.Soc.Sc (Coordinating Minister for Human Development and Culture of the Republic of Indonesia), H.E. José Antonio Morató Tavares (Ambassador of the Republic of Indonesia to the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus), Honorary Consul Valery Radchenko, and Leningrad Oblast officials (the Committee on the Environment, the Committee on External Relations, the Directorate of Specially Protected Natural Areas, and the St. Petersburg & Leningrad Oblast branch of the All-Russian Society for Nature Conservation), together with the chairs of PERMIRA and PERMIRA St. Petersburg; and the cutting of a traditional tumpeng followed by a group photo.

sections.title: Cuisine
sections.body: Cooking is the central shared activity. In the Culinary Masterclass & Cooking Sessions, mixed teams of Indonesian, Russian, and ASEAN students cook Indonesian dishes together and learn the ingredients, techniques, and cultural stories behind them. Example dishes that illustrate Indonesian culinary heritage include Ayam Lalapan, Nasi Goreng Kampung, Sate Taichan, Bubur Ayam, and Cekodok. Actual dishes may vary depending on programme arrangements and availability.

sections.title: Meals
sections.body: All meals are provided during the camp. Day 1: lunch is rice, Ayam Lalapan, and a mixed-vegetable side; dinner is Nasi Goreng Kampung. Day 2: breakfast is Bubur Ayam; lunch is the Nasi Goreng Kampung, Sate Taichan, and Sambal Matah made in the masterclass; dinner is Chicken Kiev with ginger butter, Dabu-Dabu, and mashed potato. Day 3: breakfast is Cekodok. Menus may vary. In line with the camp's environmental ethic, participants are asked to bring their own reusable cutlery and drink container and to take efficient portions to reduce food waste.

sections.title: Environmental Stewardship
sections.body: As a commitment to sustainability, participants are asked to: bring their own reusable cutlery and drink containers; take efficient food portions to reduce food waste; sort waste into three categories (organic, non-organic, and hazardous/B3 such as glass, ink, medicine, or batteries); and minimise paper and single-use plastic — including using QR codes instead of paper during games and registration.

sections.title: Registration
sections.body: Reserve a place through the website's registration form. Requirements: a valid passport; a Russian university student card (Studencheskiy Bilet / Propusk); minimum age 18 (no upper limit); status as an active university student in Russia; basic conversational English; and genuine interest in culture and cuisine with willingness to participate fully, including cooking and team activities. You upload both the passport and student card in the form. Indonesian applicants must be registered in the PERMIRA St. Petersburg database and have completed lapor diri (peduliwni.kemlu.go.id). Priority is given to Indonesian students in a Russian-language preparatory class. Selected participants are notified by email.

sections.title: Languages
sections.body: The programme is conducted in Indonesian and Russian. Basic conversational English is required of all participants to support cross-cultural interaction.

faqs.question: Where and when do we meet?
faqs.answer: On 19 July, gather at Ozerki metro station in Saint Petersburg at 09:00 MSK. Volunteers will meet you there, then the group transfers together by coach north to Cape Kiperort (Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast). Please be on time — the group leaves together.

faqs.question: Where is the camp?
faqs.answer: At Cape Kiperort, a peninsula in the Vyborgsky nature reserve (Vyborg District, Leningrad Oblast) on the shore of Vyborg Bay. It's a remote coastal reserve — pine forest with rocky and sandy shores — reached overland by coach.

faqs.question: Can I watch the opening ceremony online?
faqs.answer: Yes. The opening ceremony on 19 July (13:30–14:35 MSK) is streamed live at summercamp2026.permiraspb.org.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: Programme participation, meals, and accommodation during the camp are provided for selected participants. Details are confirmed during selection.

faqs.question: Who can join?
faqs.answer: Active university students in Russia aged 18 or over (no upper limit) from Indonesia, Russia, or ASEAN countries, with basic conversational English, a valid passport, and a Russian university student card.

faqs.question: Can ASEAN students join?
faqs.answer: Yes. Of the 35 places, 10 are reserved for students from ASEAN countries, alongside 15 Indonesian and 10 Russian participants.

faqs.question: What language is the camp in?
faqs.answer: The camp runs in Indonesian and Russian. Basic conversational English is required so everyone can interact across cultures.

faqs.question: What is the registration deadline?
faqs.answer: The exact deadline will be announced on this page and through PERMIRA St. Petersburg's channels (VK and Telegram).
